messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P-98732 fired -> eu-inference-kvcache-eviction | 429 spike across eu-prod inference pool
pagerduty-bot: ALERT: P-98732 assigned to @maya (on-call). Priority: P1. Link: https://pagerduty.example/P-98732
maya: ack'd. I'm on it. grabbing context and will triage.
infra-runbot: auto-collected logs attached: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z eu-node-3 inference_service WARN kvcache: eviction-storm, mem_pressure=0.92
2026-03-15T10:12:04Z eu-node-3 inference_service ERROR handler: request=12345 status=429 upstream=cache_miss
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z eu-loadbalancer warning: 502->429 surge on /v1/generate
```
maya: TL;DR looks like aggressive kvcache eviction causing lots of cache-miss + downstream 429s. initial metric: 2.1% failed token responses in eu for last 2m, latency x1.8
liz: customer-impact check: support surfaced 3 customers complaining about timeouts (finance-prod, chat-ops, partner-api). ETA on rollback?
tom: tagging in — on-call overlap now. maya, want me to take ownership? I can start scaling dedicated pool and toggle fallback routing to us-east.
maya: please take it, i'm mid-debug on node. handing to @tom in 3. leaving my debug notes: 
- eu-node-3 shows repeated kvcache evict loops after quantized model change yesterday
- local heap growth triggers eviction policy threshold sooner than expected
- suspect kernel selection change from rollout 2026-03-14 22:00
sophie: @tom if you spin up emergency capacity, remember to set autoscale.min_replicas=2 for dedicated-pool-eu, otherwise it will re-shrink. Also set routing policy to prefer us-east fallback with 10% sampling to avoid cold starts.
tom: starting capacity bump now. running command: 
```
redwoodctl capacity set --pool dedicated-pool-eu --replicas 6 --priority emergency
redwoodctl routing set --policy eu->us-east --pct 30 --grace 60s
```
infra-runbot: command output: 
```
OK: resized pool dedicated-pool-eu -> 6 replicas
OK: routing policy applied (30% fallback to us-east)
```
pagerduty-bot: P-98732 acknowledged by tom. Status: investigating.
maya: note: metrics show kv-eviction spikes align with model-compact cron on eu-node-3 (00:00 UTC). we had a partial config change last night that reduced kv_cache_size by 20%.
liz: customer comms: drafting short blurb for status.redwood.io — "We are investigating elevated 429 errors for EU inference traffic; mitigation in progress. No data loss reported." Any objections?
sophie: fine to publish. add: "Workaround: we are routing a subset of traffic to alternate regions to reduce impact."
tom: initial mitigation shows errors dropping to 0.7% after routing. latency stabilizing. leaving 30% traffic to us-east for 10m while we roll a hotfix.
maya: handoff complete. @tom is incident owner. i'll post the core dump and heap profile in the incident ticket.
tom: working on hotfix: increasing kvcache limit and reverting kernel-selection flag. patch will be applied to eu-node-{1,2,3} in canary then rollout. plan: canary -> 20% -> 100% over 10m.
sophie: remind to run post-deploy load-test on canary: `make perf-test TARGET=eu-node-1 RPS=2000`
infra-runbot: canary patch applied to eu-node-1 at 10:34Z. basic smoke ok.
liz: posted status update: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/P-98732 — customers notified.
tom: rolling to 20% now. monitoring logs and 429 rate.
maya: quick note for postmortem: we need tighter guardrails on kv_cache_size rollouts + automated synthetic checks for 429 regressions after kernel changes.
sophie: agreed. add rollout checklist item: "simulate cache pressure with synthetic traffic before kernel change".
infra-runbot: 429 rate back to baseline (<0.1%) at 10:46Z. routing policy reverting to normal in 120s.
tom: reverting fallback. running: `redwoodctl routing set --policy clear eu`
pagerduty-bot: P-98732 status: resolved by tom. Resolution: kv_cache sizing rollback + emergency capacity + routing fallback.
maya: thanks team. postmortem owner: @maya -> will draft within 48h. action items in ticket: ["add synthetic 429 regression test", "safeguard kv_cache rollouts", "improve canary observability"]
liz: closing customer loop now.:+1:
